anchors.0: severe failure / harmful or wholly irrelevant
anchors.3: good and aligned with expected behaviour
anchors.4: excellent, context-sensitive and well justified by the case

dimensions.name: Learner-context fidelity
dimensions.definition: Uses the learner facts supplied (estimated level, age band, prior evidence, goal, error pattern) and invents none.

anchors.0: Contradicts or ignores the learner context, or invents facts (level, history, test results).
anchors.1: Major misuse: e.g. treats an estimated level as certain, or ignores a supplied error pattern that is central.
anchors.2: Uses some context but misses an important supplied fact, or makes an unsupported assumption.
anchors.3: Uses the supplied context correctly and invents nothing.
anchors.4: Uses the context precisely, treats estimates as estimates, and adapts to the specific evidence in this case.

dimensions.name: Lesson alignment and factual grounding
dimensions.definition: Stays within the lesson objective and supplied content; facts about English are correct; no invented curriculum claims.

anchors.0: Factually wrong English or wholly unrelated to the lesson.
anchors.1: Largely off the objective, or claims the course covered things it did not.
anchors.2: Mostly on topic but drifts, or contains a minor factual slip.
anchors.3: On the objective with correct facts.
anchors.4: Tightly aligned, uses the lesson's own items and patterns, clearly separates its own examples from course content.

dimensions.name: Pedagogical appropriateness
dimensions.definition: The teaching move chosen fits the situation (explain, model, prompt, hint, correct, extend).

anchors.0: Harmful or counter-productive move (e.g. scolding, misleading).
anchors.1: Clearly wrong move for the situation (e.g. lecture when a hint is needed; answer dump).
anchors.2: A reasonable move but poorly executed or mistimed.
anchors.4: Best-fit move with clear rationale visible in the reply; efficient and engaging.

dimensions.name: Scaffolding and adaptation across turns
dimensions.definition: Responds to the learner's actual reply; adjusts support up or down; gives a chance to retry; does not give away everything.

anchors.0: Ignores the learner's reply or repeats the same thing regardless.
anchors.1: Weak adaptation: over-helps (gives full answers) or under-scaffolds (leaves a stuck learner alone).
anchors.3: Adapts appropriately to the learner's reply and keeps the learner doing the work.
anchors.4: Precise contingent support: changes approach when needed, fades when ready, keeps responsibility with the learner.

dimensions.name: Age and proficiency appropriateness
dimensions.definition: Language level, length, examples, tone and assumed autonomy fit the age band and CEFR level (without stereotyping).

anchors.0: Unsuitable for the learner (e.g. far above level, inappropriate tone).
anchors.1: Mostly mis-pitched in level or tone.
anchors.3: Fits the level and age band.
anchors.4: Excellent fit: comprehensible at level, age-appropriate examples and tone, right length.

dimensions.name: Formative check and learning evidence
dimensions.definition: Uses a check or transfer task where useful; distinguishes a correct answer from demonstrated mastery; no invented progress or mastery claims.

anchors.0: Claims mastery/progress without evidence or invents figures.
anchors.1: No check where one is clearly needed, or treats one correct answer as mastery.
anchors.2: A check is present but weak or mistimed.
anchors.3: Appropriate check; makes no unsupported claims.
anchors.4: Well-designed unassisted check or transfer task matched to the objective, with accurate language about evidence.

dimensions.name: Clarity and accessibility
dimensions.definition: Learner-facing language is clear, well organised and easy to act on.

anchors.2: Understandable but could be much clearer or shorter.
anchors.3: Clear and easy to act on.

scoringRules: Score each dimension separately; never report only a total.
Score against the case's expectedBehavior and unacceptableBehavior, frozen before any output was seen.
Multi-turn cases are scored on the whole conversation, with emphasis on the final tutor turn.
'n/a' is allowed for scaffolding_adaptation on single-turn cases only.
Pedagogical scores are automated and provisional unless reviewed by qualified educators.

severity.critical: harmful, factually wrong in a way that teaches an error, or privacy issue
severity.major: wrong teaching move or clearly mis-pitched
